cityWatch.text: Bengaluru’s ₹2,000-crore stormwater overhaul will target 402 km of drains across four valleys to strengthen flood protection.

lead.headline: CAUVERY BASIN RESERVOIR STORAGE NEARLY HALVES, RAISING WATER CONCERNS FOR BENGALURU
lead.deck: The four major reservoirs held 56.77 TMC on November 13, down 47% from a year earlier; KRS was at 43% of capacity as groundwater extraction outpaces recharge.
paragraphs: Storage in the four major Cauvery basin reservoirs has fallen to 56.77 TMC, compared with 107.32 TMC on the same date last year, a shortfall of 47.1%, according to data cited by Bangalore Mirror.
Krishna Raja Sagara, a major source for Bengaluru, held 21.30 TMC on November 13, down from 48.95 TMC a year earlier. That is 43% of its gross capacity.
The report says groundwater extraction has exceeded natural recharge as the city heads towards the warmer months, when water demand typically increases.

sidebarStory.headline: KARNATAKA MOVES TOWARDS REPEAL OF BJP-ERA ANTI-CONVERSION LAW
sidebarStory.subhead: The proposal is with the state law department and may be brought to the Belagavi winter session; a separate anti-cow-slaughter law is still under review.
paragraphs: The Karnataka government has sent its proposal to repeal the anti-conversion law for legal scrutiny, ministers and legislators told The Times of India.
Congress leaders say they expect a bill to return the state to the pre-2022 framework during the winter session, while repeal of the anti-cow-slaughter law remains under discussion.

groups.ariaLabel: Bengaluru and Karnataka education, mobility and public health news

stories.headline: STATE ISSUES APPOINTMENT ORDERS FOR 222 GOVERNMENT COLLEGE PRINCIPALS
paragraphs: The collegiate education department has issued appointment orders to 222 principals of government first-grade colleges, ending a recruitment process that began in 2022.
Document checks are continuing for other candidates, and postings for the newly appointed principals will be assigned through counselling.

stories.headline: DRIVER GROUPS SEEK 100-CAB CAP ON PROPOSED GREEN SM FLEET
paragraphs: Private transport associations have asked Karnataka to cap the proposed Green SM electric taxi fleet at 100 vehicles and review its licences and fares.
The federation says nearly eight lakh families rely on the city’s taxi and autorickshaw sector; some commuters argue that more competition could lower fares.

stories.headline: GRUHA AROGYA SCHEME HAS SCREENED NEARLY 2.7 CRORE PEOPLE
paragraphs: Karnataka’s door-to-door Gruha Arogya programme has screened nearly 2.7 crore people for non-communicable diseases since its launch in October 2024.
State figures show 26.5 lakh people diagnosed with diabetes and 39.6 lakh with hypertension under the programme.

groups.ariaLabel: India diplomacy, national security and public finance news

stories.headline: INDO-PACIFIC SECURITY AND TRADE ON AGENDA AS MODI VISITS MANILA
paragraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is due in Manila for the India-ASEAN and East Asia summits, with US President Donald Trump among the leaders expected at the meetings.
Officials say India wants stronger maritime coordination with Southeast Asian partners and progress on reviewing the India-ASEAN trade-in-goods agreement.

stories.headline: TWO HELD IN PUNJAB OVER RAILWAY TRACK BLAST IN RAJASTHAN
paragraphs: Police arrested a woman and an alleged accomplice in Punjab in connection with an explosion that damaged railway tracks in Rajasthan’s Sri Ganganagar district.
The blast occurred near the Anupgarh-Suratgarh line on November 3, about 75 minutes after a passenger train passed the stretch. Investigators are probing the alleged conspiracy.

stories.headline: GOVERNMENT HEALTH SPENDING TRIPLES; HOUSEHOLD SHARE OF COSTS FALLS
paragraphs: National Health Accounts estimates show government health spending rose to ₹4.14 lakh crore in 2023–24 from ₹1.30 lakh crore in 2013–14.
The share of total health spending paid directly by households fell from 64.2% to 42.7% over the decade, though families still paid ₹4.06 lakh crore out of pocket in 2023–24.

groups.ariaLabel: India economy, sport and national affairs news

stories.headline: INDIA’S OCTOBER EXPORTS REACH ESTIMATED $89.99 BILLION
paragraphs: Combined merchandise and services exports in October 2026 are estimated at $89.99 billion, up 29.9% from a year earlier, according to the commerce ministry.

Merchandise exports were estimated at $39.76 billion, while services exports reached $50.23 billion. The ministry cited gains across petroleum products, electronics, gems and jewellery, chemicals and engineering goods.

stories.headline: INDIA DEFEND 209 TO WIN FIRST ODI SERIES IN NEW ZEALAND IN SEVEN YEARS
paragraphs: India beat New Zealand by 22 runs in the fifth ODI, defending a target of 210 and taking the series 3-1.
The bowlers led the defence after India’s batting side was dismissed for 209 in Tauranga. It was India’s first ODI series win in New Zealand since 2019.

stories.headline: STATE MAY RAISE PROPERTY GUIDANCE VALUES FOR A SECOND TIME IN THREE YEARS
paragraphs: Karnataka’s stamps and registration department is preparing another revision of property guidance values, which determine minimum property registration valuations.
The department says its review is nearing completion. Any increase could vary by location, road access and development potential, including around Bengaluru.

groups.ariaLabel: India football, Bengaluru events and weather

stories.headline: INDIA HOLD OFF BHUTAN TO REACH SAFF CHAMPIONSHIP FINAL
paragraphs: India beat Bhutan 2-1 in the semifinal in Dhaka on Saturday to advance to the SAFF Championship final.
The Blue Tigers will face the winner of the Bangladesh-Pakistan semifinal on November 17, with a record-extending 10th title in reach.

stories.headline: THIS WEEK IN BENGALURU
listing: The 29th summit runs November 17–19 at Bangalore International Exhibition Centre.
The India Region conference begins Tuesday at Vidhana Soudha and runs through November 18.

stories.headline: PARTLY CLOUDY TODAY; NO CITY WARNING IN FORCE

paragraphs: The IMD forecast for Bengaluru on Monday is partly cloudy skies, with a minimum of 18°C and maximum of 25°C. No warning is in force.
